research_rationale:
Executive Order 13551 of 2010-08-30 (75 FR 53837, PDF pages 1-4) is held as the Federal Register original (govinfo PDF text layer, grade official original). I read it in full and confirm its identity and its clause inventory of 25 scopes as prepared (a dup2 suffix distinguishes repeated item labels in different subsections). Its authority is IEEPA, the NEA and the other statutes it names, and it rests on the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13466 of June 26, 2008, expanded in scope by Executive Order 13551. Notice of June 22, 2026 (91 FR 38231; FR Doc. 2026-12836) states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond June 26, 2026, so the emergency, and the order that depends on it, were in effect on the cutoff of 2026-10-14 (NEA section 202(d)). Earlier annual continuation notices for the same emergency are also held; the latest one is relied on because it speaks as of its date. The held original has no own-terms end, expiry or sunset. I read the coverage notes of current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point through 2026-10-09), current-law:ecfr (as of 2026-10-14) and later-events:ofr_catalog (checked 2026-11-25); they show no revocation, supersession or partial revocation of this order. The Federal Register disposition notes for this order contain cross-reference entries only, naming EO 13466, EO 13570, EO 13687, EO 13810 and annual continuation notices (June 13, 2022; June 20, 2025; June 22, 2026), none of which is stated to revoke or supersede this order. No later instrument amends or revokes any clause. The dossier gaps listed as NOTICE identities absent from the census are annual continuation notices and cross-references, not events that change this order; the current-law pointer gaps concern CFR and Code pointers that this claim does not rely on, because the conclusion rests on the order's own text and the continuation notice. The acting-text lead for Executive Order 14294 (Fighting Overcriminalization in Federal Regulations, May 9, 2025) was checked: a scan of the held corpus found no mention of this order in its text, so no provision targeting this order was located. OFAC designation notices held among the acting texts (for example the Notice of OFAC Sanctions Action at 90 FR 51441) were issued under section 1(a)(ii)(F) of this order in November 2025, which is consistent with, but not a basis for, the conclusion that the order continues. Later orders EO 13570, EO 13687 and EO 13810 recite this order or the emergency; they are recitals, not amendments or revocations (their texts were read for the clauses that cite it). Savings: none arises because the order remained in force at the cutoff.
